# Phobos Agriculture: equipment and item reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/update-item-reference.ps1. Edit config/item-reference.json, not this file. -->

Current source candidate: **0.64.0**. Game target: **1.0.1.5**. Values below come from offline definitions; they do not establish installation, gameplay validation or a live merchant quote.

Verdemorrow equipment grows potatoes and lettuce, cooks potato portions and manages finite irrigation. These are authored, accelerated gameplay systems. Crop yields and simplified nutrient/treatment chemistry are not research results. The linked research guide attributes the supporting work separately; none of the pricing or yield balance implies NASA/ESA endorsement. See [research and attribution](development/agriculture-research.md). Regional offers extend through the current vanilla solar system; see [market coverage and the game's market pricing](solar-system-economy.md). Crew standing orders are opt-in; see [crew work, training and time-skips](crew-automation.md) for eligible work, approved stores, resource limits and resuming industrial and exterior work. Compact controls, unsaved settings and object selection are explained in the [control-panel guide](control-panel-guide.md). In selection fields, Locate opens a temporary marked ship view; Clear is a draft change that requires Apply. Pick on ship marks eligible objects and Escape restores the panel and view.

**Reading prices:** credits per complete object at the stated condition, before shop margins, market effects, negotiation and extra wear. Pristine retail can cost more. Mass is the empty/dry definition or fresh commodity template; saved contents and variable recovery packets can weigh differently. Dismantle value is the sum of all listed outputs at base value, excluding labour and tools.

**Repair and Restore:** Repair fixes a damaged form and uses up its parts, as the game's own repairs do. Restore reduces wear on functional equipment in place; it does not grant pristine status. Empty cargo and follow the machine’s local maintenance guards first. Work speed depends on crew, tools and current condition.

**Finding stock:** the generated percentages are defaults per eligible native stock/loot roll, not per ship or guaranteed shop availability. Offers are additive, may be independent, and require normal restocking. Merchant offers request the listed finite lot when successful; separate world-loot branches retain their own listed quantities. Configuration, capacity and native generation rules still apply; loading an existing save does not refill its inventories.

**Stacking:** limits below apply to loose items on the ground or in compatible containers; 1 means no multi-item stack. Installed equipment remains individual. Limits count objects, not kilograms, and do not change merchant lot sizes or per-object contents.

## Firstlight-4 Cultivation Rack

Grows one potato, food-lettuce or lettuce-seed cohort across four visual trays.

**Use:** Install and power the rack, load irrigation and nutrients, then perform Plant. Keep cabin conditions suitable and Harvest when ready. In a room too hot for the crop, Mist to cool crop holds it up to 4 C below the room for about 0.15 kg of water an hour per degree, and halves the heat damage beyond that; it also cools the room a little. Remove output cargo before replanting. Supported crew work is configured through the [standing-order controls](crew-automation.md); orders begin disabled and retain the existing access and supply requirements.

**Where it appears:** Buy equipment or build at a supported table; used/refurbished/damaged offers are listed below. This item may also appear in eligible engineering-equipment loot; see the exact offers below. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Warm standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Four trays are one crop batch. Food lettuce does not return seeds; choose the dedicated seed cycle. The local panel shows inventory, stress and progress.

Full operating instructions: [Firstlight-4 Cultivation Rack guide](agriculture-player-guide.md).

## Hearth-2 Galley Cooker

Cooks a raw potato portion into edible prepared food.

**Use:** Install, power, place raw potatoes in its Inventory and Start. Collect the cooked portion when complete. Supported crew work is configured through the [standing-order controls](crew-automation.md); orders begin disabled and retain the existing access and supply requirements.

**Where it appears:** Buy equipment or build at a supported table. This item may also appear in eligible engineering-equipment loot; see the exact offers below. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Warm standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Its counter and stove artwork are one machine. Each job binds a particular raw portion; replacing it does not transfer progress.

Full operating instructions: [Hearth-2 Galley Cooker guide](agriculture-player-guide.md).

<a id="supply"></a>

## Groundwork W2 Water Supply Unit

Stores water and nutrients and feeds both to its linked racks; also treats recorded process solution.

**Use:** Install and power W2, load water locally, link its racks and Start. Put any Groundwork nutrients in its Inventory, or set a nutrient hopper within one tile: it takes them by itself and feeds them with the water, recirculating a full rack's water when needed. Nothing is chosen, paused or unlinked. Use treatment controls for recorded drainage and a cartridge. Supported crew work is configured through the [standing-order controls](crew-automation.md); orders begin disabled and retain the existing access and supply requirements. A drain canister of water put in its inventory pours into its reservoir.

**Where it appears:** Buy supply/fixer/Halvorson stock or build at a supported table. This item may also appear in eligible engineering-equipment loot; see the exact offers below. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Warm standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

One nutrient for every crop since Agriculture 0.55.0: it keeps each rack at 0.1 kg, up to 10 g with each kilogram of water moved. Feeds mixed by earlier versions convert by themselves into water and nutrients. Several W2s may share one irrigation pipe; a W2 within one tile of its rack feeds it without the pipe. Receiving and pumping that were running carry on after a reload. Optional [Valtora’s Ship’s Water](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3757331189) integration is version-scoped and protects crew reserves; manual input remains available.

Full operating instructions: [Groundwork W2 Water Supply Unit guide](fluid-network-operations.md).

<a id="irrigation-pipe"></a>

## Groundwork Irrigation Conduit

Carries irrigation water, and the nutrients fed with it, between W2 and paired racks.

**Use:** Place contiguous segments in MISC from under or right beside the W2 to under or right beside each rack (any side), then use Pair/Receive controls; a W2 within one tile of a rack needs no pipe. A running W2 fills it first, about 0.2 kg of water a tile; to take it up, right-click it and choose Drain line into canister with a Framework drain canister carried or within two tiles.

**Where it appears:** Buy stock, build at a supported table, or find a loose segment in eligible locked-crate contents. This item may also appear in eligible engineering-equipment loot; see the exact offers below. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks, at any standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → MISC. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Separate from electricity and F6 coolant. Since Agriculture 0.33.0 each tile holds its own water and cannot be taken up until drained; feed left in it by a version before 0.55.0 is flushed into the W2 when it next runs, or drains as before; a line parcel saved by an earlier version is delivered into its rack on the next powered run. Loose intact and damaged sections support storage stacks, separately by identity; installed segments remain individual fixtures. Split off a section when an action requires an individual item.

Full operating instructions: [Groundwork Irrigation Conduit guide](agriculture-water-conduits.md).

<a id="seed-potato"></a>

## Continuance Seed Potato

Planting stock for a potato crop.

**Use:** Place one in the rack and choose Plant potato after loading water and nutrients.

**Where it appears:** Buy stock, find eligible fridge/crate loot, or retain stock from a potato harvest. See the listed merchant offers for current retail availability. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks, at any standing.

**Placement:** Inventory/module-slot item; no standalone INSTALL entry.

This is the sprouted planting item, not a raw edible portion. Split off one seed potato or seed packet before manual planting; an intact stack is not a planting input. Crew source hauling can deliver individual units from stacks.

Full operating instructions: [Continuance Seed Potato guide](agriculture-player-guide.md).

## Continuance Seed Wheat

<a id="workup-bench"></a>

## Groundwork B2 Workup Bench

Recovers recorded crop nutrients and formulates finite W2 mixtures.

**Use:** Install through APPS, power, load a recorded residue packet, prepare recovery and Start. Then prepare recovered concentrate plus equal-mass makeup salts and Start. Leave output room. Supported crew work is configured through the [standing-order controls](crew-automation.md); orders begin disabled and retain the existing access and supply requirements.

**Where it appears:** Buy supply/fixer/Halvorson stock or construct at a supported table. This item may also appear in eligible engineering-equipment loot; see the exact offers below. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Warm standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Each stage binds physical inputs and consumes power; a stage that was running carries on after a reload. Damaged hardware is repairable; consumable contents are not.

Full operating instructions: [Groundwork B2 Workup Bench guide](agriculture-nutrient-production.md).

<a id="bulk-reservoir"></a>

## Groundwork R3, R4 and R5 Agricultural Water Reservoirs

Retired in Agriculture 0.31.0. The former agricultural water buffers (120 kg in the 3 x 3 R3, 235 kg in the 4 x 4 R4, 400 kg in the 5 x 5 R5) convert on load to Framework's Rivetline S3, S4 and S5 process water silos of the same footprint.

**Use:** Nothing to do: every saved reservoir, installed or loose, becomes the silo of its size when the game loads, in place, with its water, reserve, inventory and W2 link. Use the silo as before; its Control Panel is Framework's, and the reservoir crew work (load a charge, recover, drain, standing fill order) carries on there.

**Where it appears:** No longer sold or found. The definitions stay only as conversion sources for jobs saved against a reservoir.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

The conversion keeps the water record under the silo's names, carries wear and locks, and moves the saved mass by the difference in housing, so the converted silo weighs and is worth what a silo is. Downgrading afterwards is not supported.

Full operating instructions: [Groundwork R3, R4 and R5 Agricultural Water Reservoirs guide](agriculture-bulk-storage.md).

<a id="nutrient-hopper"></a>

## Groundwork E2, E3 and E4 Nutrient Hoppers

Passive stores of formulated dry crop nutrients, kept as a kilogram record: 10 kg in the 2 x 2 E2, 25 kg in the 3 x 3 E3 and 48 kg in the 4 x 4 E4. A W2 within one tile stocks its nutrient store from one while running.

**Use:** Install through APPS within one tile of a W2. Fill it at a station refuelling kiosk under Bulk supplies (crop nutrients by the kilogram at 1,500 cr/kg). A W2 with no charge in its Inventory uses the hopper by itself; its Supplies page names the source. Crew work recovers trapped nutrients after repair and bags up to 500 g at a time into a bulk nutrient charge to empty it. See [the bulk storage guide](agriculture-bulk-storage.md).

**Where it appears:** Empty loose hardware on the reservoir routes (Agriculture supply, fixer, Halvorson and supported regional merchants), finite lots of four. No fabrication recipe. The E2 may also appear in eligible engineering-equipment loot; the E3 and E4 never do. See the exact offers below. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks; they ask Warm standing.

**Placement:** INSTALL → APPS. Obtain the loose item first; the menu does not manufacture it.

Damage isolates the nutrients in a finite catch until repaired and recovered; nothing leaks. A hopper holding nutrients refuses to be moved or dismantled. Kiosk nutrients cost the same per kilogram as bulk charges and packets, and nothing sells back. The contents are the crop model's single aggregate nutrient figure.

Full operating instructions: [Groundwork E2, E3 and E4 Nutrient Hoppers guide](agriculture-bulk-storage.md).

<a id="bulk-nutrients"></a>

## Groundwork Bulk Nutrient Charge

One physical 500 g dry formulated nutrient charge for gradual selected W2 dosing.

**Use:** Put in the W2 inventory; the W2 takes nutrients from it by itself while running. Explicitly choose the distribute-and-replace standing order to authorize crew replacement from the approved input store.

**Where it appears:** Agriculture merchants in finite lots of eight, or one charge per independent station Bulk supplies purchase into a selected W2 inventory. Also sold for scrip at the CCRE and GalCon faction kiosks, at any standing.

**Placement:** Inventory/module-slot item; no standalone INSTALL entry.

Same aggregate formulation value per kg as existing nutrients. Dedicated bulk nutrient packet artwork, localized name and measured mass distinguish it. No water carrier or new chemical assay. Remaining mass/value decrease; empty charges vanish. No Repair/Restore. Bulk charges support storage stacks of three individual objects. Split off one before dosing; partially depleted charges retain their own contents.

## Evidence and upkeep

Item names, dry/template masses, prices, service bills, salvage outputs, placement tabs, stock probabilities and table recipes are generated from current Phobos definitions. **Blue Bottle Games’ Ostranauts** native `DataCO.GetBasePrice` supplies the offline valuation used here ([developer’s game page](https://bluebottlegames.com/games/ostranauts)). That page identifies the game; the actual numeric evidence is the locally inspected assembly, whose hash is retained in the generated data snapshot. No proprietary source or game assembly is distributed.

Function/use explanations are maintained in the reviewed catalogue. All fictional prices, yields and simplified processing are Phobos gameplay choices. Research attribution remains beside the relevant claims in the linked operating/research guides. See [reference maintenance](development/item-reference-maintenance.md) for the one-click updater and coverage checks.
